newsitem.title: USA: Viacom asks studios to cut video prices-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Viacom asks studios to cut video prices-WSJ.

text.p: Viacom Inc Chairman Sumner Redstone has asked movie studios to cut the prices of videos they sell to its Blockbuster video-store chain by as much as 15 percent, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal said that Redstone has sought that and other concessions from suppliers in a recent visit to Hollywood studios, arguing it was in the movie industry's best interests to help Blockbuster.
"The video business is what makes movie industry economics work these days," an unnamed executive close to Viacom said. "If they kill the golden goose, they will have problems."
Studio executives said Redstone suggested Blockbuster might buy fewer videos from the studios if they did not agree to the concessions.
In the meetings, Redstone has suggested that the price cuts be retroactive to the beginning of the year.
But his proposals are getting a cool reception.
"He proposed new terms that were a complete loss for us and a gain for him," one executive said.
